newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BICHEL TAKES 5-46 TO PUT LEADERS QUEENSLAND ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BICHEL TAKES 5-46 TO PUT LEADERS QUEENSLAND ON TOP.

text.p: Queensland pace bowler Andrew Bichel, who shone against the West Indian touring team recently, took five wickets to help dismiss Victoria for a paltry 162 in their Sheffield Shield match in Brisbane on Friday.
Bichel finished with five for 46 as Shield leaders Queensland took charge on the opening day of the four-day game. They were 100 for one at the close, with Trevor Barsby unbeaten on 51.

Victoria capitulated after former Australia batsman and acting captain Dean Jones, leading the side while skipper Shane Warne is on test duty against West Indies and regular stand-in Tony Dodemaide is injured, won the toss and opted to bat.
Jones was immediately made to rue his decision as Bichel, who helped an Australian XI beat West Indies by 10 wickets in Hobart 11 days ago, took the wickets of Victoria's top four batsmen.
In Hobart, deposed Australia opener Michael Slater was top scorer for New South Wales with 76 against Tasmania.

Slater, discarded for the first two tests against West Indies, dragged his side out of early trouble for New South Wales to be 263 for eight at the close. Brad McNamara was the only other batsman to offer significant resistance and was 54 not out.
In Adelaide, all-rounder Joe Scuderi (55) led South Australia from a shaky 150 for five to 277 all out against Western Australia, who were six without loss at the close.
